newsitem.title: ITALY: Saudi-owned Orbit to broadcast in Tunisia.
newsitem.headline: Saudi-owned Orbit to broadcast in Tunisia.

text.p: Orbit Satellite Television and Radio Network, a Saudi-owned relay station based in Rome, said on Friday it had obtained approval from Tunisia to broadcast in the North African country.
Orbit said in a statement that the Ministry of Information in Tunis had granted it "the right to register its company and distribute its sophisticated digital receivers" in the country.
Viewers would receive a specially tailored selection of the network's more than 30 TV and radio channels.
"Orbit has long considered the Maghreb to be a market of considerable strategic significane," Allan F. Garner, Orbit senior vice president of operations, said in the statement.
"This approval marks an important step forward in our commitment to delivering digital services, paving the way for direct access to the marketplace," he said.
Orbit, wholly-owned by the Mawarid Group of Saudi Arabia, is a 24-hour digital, multi-channel pay-television service that broadcasts to 23 countries.

The company announced last month that it would launch a specially tailored Disney Channel to the Middle East and Africa on April 2, 1997. Industry sources said the programming would respect cultural and religious sensitivities.
